# tidytuesdayR

tidytuesdayR makes it easy to participate in the weekly
[`#TidyTuesday`](https://tidytues.day/) project by providing functions
to quickly import data posted to the [Tidy Tuesday
repository](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday).

## Installation

This package is (usually) available on CRAN via:

``` r
install.packages("tidytuesdayR")
```

To get the latest in-development features, install the development
version from GitHub:

``` r
#install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("dslc-io/tidytuesdayR")
```

## Usage

There are currently two methods to access the data from the respository.

### Load the Data!

The simplest way is to use the
[`tt_load()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/tt_load.md)
function. This function has accepts two types of inputs to determine
which data to grab. It can be a date as a string in the YYYY-MM-DD
format like below.

``` r
library(tidytuesdayR)
tt_data <- tt_load("2019-01-15")
```

Or the function can accept the year as the first argument, and which
week of the year as the second.

``` r
tt_data <- tt_load(2019, week=3) 
```

[`tt_load()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/tt_load.md)
naively downloads *all* the data that is available and stores them in
the resulting `tt_data` object. To access the data, use the `$` or `[[`
notation and the name of the dataset.

``` r
tt_data$agencies
tt_data[["agencies"]]
```

To view the readme, either print the `tt_data` object or use the
[`readme()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/readme.md)
function. When you print the `tt_data` object, you also get the
available datasets names printed in the console.

``` r
readme(tt_data)
print(tt_data)
```

``` R
## Available Datasets:
##  agencies 
##  launches 
##  
```

### TidyTemplate

As part of the goal of making participating in \#TidyTuesday easier,
{tidytuesdayR} now also provides a template! To use it, just use the
[`use_tidytemplate()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/use_tidytemplate.md)
function!

By default, the template will assume to be using the most recent
TidyTuesday. However, you can pass a date object or character string in
YYYY-MM-DD format defining a different date you want to use. If you
don’t recall the exact date, no worries, you can use the
[`tt_available()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/tt_available.md)
function to figure out which date and get the date to use!

``` r
## this weeks TidyTuesday!
tidytuesdayR::use_tidytemplate()

## TidyTuesday from Week 42 of 2019
tidytuesdayR::use_tidytemplate(refdate = "2019-10-15")
```

Additionally, by default the template will create the new file in your
working directory, using the “YYYY_MM_DD” format per good practices.
However, if you are so inclined, you can rename it to whatever you wish.

``` r
tidytuesdayR::use_tidytemplate(name = "My Super Great TidyTuesday.Rmd")
```

## Contributing

Please note that the ‘tidytuesdayR’ project is released with a
[Contributor Code of
Conduct](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). By
contributing to this project, you agree to abide by its terms.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`last_tuesday()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/last_tuesday.md)
  : Find the most recent tuesday
- [`print(`*`<tt_data>`*`)`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/printing.md)
  [`print(`*`<tt>`*`)`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/printing.md)
  : print methods of the tt objects
- [`readme()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/readme.md)
  : Readme HTML maker and Viewer
- [`tt_available()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/tt_available.md)
  [`tt_datasets()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/tt_available.md)
  : Listing all available TidyTuesdays
- [`tt_clean()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/tt_clean.md)
  : Create and open cleaning.R
- [`tt_curate_data()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/tt_curate_data.md)
  : Guidance for TidyTuesday dataset curation
- [`tt_download()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/tt_download.md)
  : Download TidyTuesday data
- [`tt_download_file()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/tt_download_file.md)
  : Download a TidyTuesday dataset file
- [`tt_intro()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/tt_intro.md)
  : Create and open intro.md
- [`tt_load()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/tt_load.md)
  : Load TidyTuesday data from Github
- [`tt_load_gh()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/tt_load_gh.md)
  : Load TidyTuesday data from Github
- [`tt_meta()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/tt_meta.md)
  : Create and open meta.yaml
- [`print(`*`<tt_dataset_table>`*`)`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/tt_print.md)
  [`print(`*`<tt_dataset_table_list>`*`)`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/tt_print.md)
  : Printing Utilities for Listing Available Datasets
- [`tt_save_dataset()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/tt_save_dataset.md)
  : Save datasets for submission
- [`tt_submit()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/tt_submit.md)
  : Submit a TidyTuesday dataset
- [`use_tidytemplate()`](https://dslc-io.github.io/tidytuesdayR/reference/use_tidytemplate.md)
  : Create and open the tidytemplate
